title: Which Theft Charge Fits?
summary: Theft, shoplifting, robbery, burglary or receiving stolen property.
note: Helps you find the right statute to read. It does not replace the statute, your prosecutor's guidance or department policy. Not yet verified against official sources.

force.q: During the theft or the immediate flight, did the suspect use force, cause injury, or threaten immediate injury?
force.help: Includes a shoplifter who shoves the guard while running out the door.

armed.q: Was the suspect armed with or did they threaten a deadly weapon, or cause or try to cause serious bodily injury?

entry.q: Did the suspect enter, or hide in, a structure with purpose to commit an offense inside?
entry.help: A house, garage, business, vehicle used as a dwelling, or a separately secured part of one.

store.q: Was it merchandise taken from a store or business offering it for sale?

recv.q: Did the suspect receive, keep or sell property they knew (or believed) was stolen, rather than take it themselves?

car.q: Was a vehicle taken just to use it, with no plan to keep it?

points: Recover the weapon, or document the threat in the victim's words.
Add weapons charges as they apply.
Force or threat during the theft, the attempt or the immediate flight turns a theft into a robbery.
Nothing has to actually be taken; an attempted theft counts.
2nd degree if they caused, tried or threatened bodily injury, or were armed.
Charge the theft or other crime inside separately.
No purpose to commit a crime inside? Look at criminal trespass instead.
Under $200 DP, $200 to $500 4th degree, over $500 3rd degree, $75,000 or more 2nd degree.
Use the full retail value. Run the shoplifting checklist.

r_rsp.result: Receiving stolen property 2C:20-7: graded by value
points: Graded by value, the same as theft.
Look for the statutory presumptions of knowledge, like a very low price paid.

r_joy.result: Unlawful taking of a means of conveyance 2C:20-10
points: For a vehicle used and abandoned without intent to keep it.
If they meant to keep it, it is theft, and a motor vehicle is 3rd degree regardless of value.

r_theft.result: Theft by unlawful taking 2C:20-3: graded by value

A firearm, motor vehicle, boat, horse, companion animal or CDS is 3rd degree regardless of value.
